subject: Draft SLA: availability slabs and proportional remedy tiers
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@stellarsys.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SLA: availability slabs and proportional remedy tiers

Jane — great to meet earlier this week. As promised, attaching our initial SLA draft for Stellar Systems that tries to balance predictable uptime guarantees with a proportional credit model that scales with impact. High-level summary: 

- Baseline availability: 99.95% for core / sync endpoints (API surface used in customer-facing requests).
- Secondary availability: 99.5% for batch/async pipelines and non-critical job queues.
- Remedy model: monthly service credits calculated as a percentage of the monthly invoice for the affected service slab; credits escalate by slab (e.g., 0.5%/1.5%/5% for <99.95, <99.5, <99.0 respectively).
- Credit cap: proposed 15% of the affected service monthly spend, with carveouts for scheduled maintenance and provider region outages documented in Section 4.
- Latency: not included in credit calculation in this draft; latency remedies handled via operational runbook and rollback/traffic-shifting commitments.

We included a small operational compromise: a 90-day "onboarding ramp" where credits are capped at 10% while we optimize prefix caching and routing for your peak flows. Also call out that Dedicated capacity purchases can get tighter SLOs (we can include guaranteed throughput lanes).

For next steps: please review pages 2–4 (remedy bands + examples) and let us know any hard constraints (e.g., must-have uptime floor, maximum monthly credit as a percent of invoice). If helpful, propose a short legal + ops sync next week and we can walk through real invoice examples.

Attachment: SLA_proposal_v1.pdf

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@stellarsys.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@stellarsys.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: availability slabs and proportional remedy tiers

Rafael — thanks for the draft and the clear breakdown. A few immediate concerns from our side: 

- Stellar’s procurement floor is 99.9% for any customer-facing API that serves transaction-critical requests. 99.95 is attractive, but we need to understand how you measure "core" endpoints and what scope we can lock down to qualify.
- Credit cap: 15% of monthly spend is high for our finance team; they want a hard cap at 10% for the first 12 months.
- Latency: latency matters to us — especially P95 for queries under 300ms. Even if you don’t want latency credits, we will need measurable latency SLOs and an operational escalation path with remediation timelines.

Also attaching a short spreadsheet with our security and audit asks (SOC2 artifacts, encryption in transit and at rest, and certs). Please confirm what artifacts you can provide.

Attachment: Stellar_security_requirements.xlsx

Jane Liu
Head of IT Operations, Stellar Systems
jane.liu@stellarsys.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@stellarsys.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: availability slabs and proportional remedy tiers

Jane — appreciate the clear feedback. A few proposals to bridge the gap that should be acceptable to finance and ops: 

1) Scoped uptime definition: we will define "core endpoints" by API paths + hostnames used in Stellar’s production routing table (we can capture this in a mutual action plan). Those endpoints will be held to 99.95% availability. Non-core (batch, analytics, internal worker) will remain at 99.5%.

2) Credit cap & ramp: agree to a 10% credit cap for months 1–3 (onboarding period) and 12% cap months 4–12. After month 12, standard cap of 15% applies unless otherwise negotiated. This gives Stellar protection during ramp without locking us into a permanent lower cap.

3) Latency commitments: we will add explicit P95 latency targets for core endpoints (example: P95 < 350ms for read operations under the assumed request size) and include operational SLAs (investigation and mitigation timelines). Latency will be monitored and reported via the Console dashboard; we propose that latency be a separate runbook item and not part of the monetary credit bands to avoid double-counting incidents.

4) Maintenance & carveouts: Scheduled maintenance windows (48–72 hours per quarter max, with at least 72h notice and a postmaint timeline) will be excluded from availability calculations. Region-level provider incidents will be eligible for mitigation credits but will also allow temporary routing to an alternate region per the smart routing policy.

Next steps I propose: Legal to redline Section 4 (remedy + caps) and Ops to exchange the API list by EOD Friday so we can lock the scope. I’ve added a link to the HubSpot deal with the high-level commercial terms for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-3891

Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jane Liu <jane.liu@stellarsys.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: availability slabs and proportional remedy tiers

Thanks — quick note to confirm next steps from our side: 

- Legal: we will send a redline of the SLA with the 10%/12%/15% cap language and carveouts called out (target 48 hours).
- Ops: Rafael, please share the production API list and peak window metrics; Jane, if you can get those to us by Friday we will have the scope locked for SLA measurement.
- Meeting: propose a joint sync with Legal + Procurement + Ops on Friday 17 Sep at 10:00am PT. If that works for Stellar, send a calendar invite and we’ll add Darwin from Infra and my contracts lead.

On the SOC2 artifacts: Rafael — can you confirm which artifacts we can safely share (certified report, controls matrix) and indicate any NDAs required?

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
